Hi Samira / Tom — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned:

Summary of needs:
- High throughput product search/embedding generation for customer-facing search (peak ~120 req/s, median latency target <200ms)
- Data residency requirement: primary US region, potential requirement for VPC/private deployment for PII-sensitive features
- Mix of bursty traffic and predictable nightly indexing jobs
- Strong preference for predictable costs for budgeting (team asked about reserved capacity vs per-token)

Qualification notes:
- Current traffic: ~30k embeddings/day today, projected to 3-5x in 6 months with new features
- Legal/security: SOC2 in progress; may require customer-managed KMS if we go private
- Timeline: pilot in Q2, production in Q3

Recommended evaluation scope:
1) Hosted API baseline (fastest to ship) — per-token pricing, can add prefix caching & batching for cost reduction.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput and cost with monthly commits; good if sustained peak is confirmed.
3) Private VPC/on-prem — for strict data residency + KMS, higher operational lead time and minimum commit.

Next steps
- I will pull together a simple cost model comparing per-token hosted vs. reserved GPU capacity vs. private deployment assumptions.
- Can you confirm: 1) whether PII will be stored in embeddings? 2) expected sustained qps and acceptable max latency?

If that looks right, I’ll loop in Aditya and Marissa to run a cost comparison and share a one-pager you can circulate with finance.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

- Sustained qps: Right now sustained is ~30 req/s for embeddings during business hours, but with new features our product team expects sustained ~100 req/s and spikes to 180-200 req/s during peak campaigns. Nightly indexing runs for full-catalog (1.2M items) that can be batch-processed over a few hours.
- Budget: Finance prefers a predictable monthly number; per-token is fine for pilot, but they’ll push for reserved commits if production looks sustained.

Would appreciate the model you mentioned — especially a side-by-side of hosted per-token with realistic caching assumptions vs dedicated reserved capacity.

Stephanie — attaching the initial model and one-pager. Highlights:

Attached:
- ACME_deployment_cost_model_v1.xlsx (breakdown)
- redwood_deployment_options_onepager.pdf

Quick summary (numbers are monthly estimates and include conservative assumptions):
- Hosted API (per-token): $12,400/mo — assumes 60% cache hit rate for repeated queries, avg 350 tokens/request, modest batching on embeddings. Good for pilot; cost scales linearly with usage and is lowest upfront.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $8,600/mo — assumes a 3-node reserved GPU pool sized to sustain 100 req/s with headroom for bursts via short-term burst capacity. Includes amortized reserved commit discount. Lower unit cost at scale but requires monthly commit and 4-6 week provisioning if not already available.
- Private VPC/on-prem: $22,000/mo effective (includes support/ops premium + KMS integration) — recommended only if Acme requires customer-managed keys and on-prem control. Higher minimums and longer lead time.

Key assumptions (included in spreadsheet):
- Batching factor: 1.8x token efficiency for throughput path
- Cache hit: 60% for popular queries, 20% for long-tail
- Embedding indexing: nightly job roughly 24 GPU-hours (can be distributed) — cost shown as amortized monthly.

Next steps I propose:
1) Stephanie: share the attachments with Acme and set a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk the numbers with Tom + finance.
2) We schedule a technical call with infra/ops if they want to explore Private VPC KMS details.
3) If they like dedicated economics, we can prepare a draft reserved commit term sheet (monthly commit + burst policy).

Let me know if you want tweaks to assumptions before I finalize v2.

Thanks,
